v3.note: Sapper's Path v3 rules and palette (SPEC-v3). Holding spaces and archer lethality per difficulty (rules: turn these after playtest); MATS order is the material id (1-14) the grid letters a-n name. v4 M1 retuned the colours for distance (tools/palette.js, report in tools/v4-m1-palette.md): every pair of materials that stand together in a level is 25+ apart in CIEDE2000. Gilt (keys) is a dark old gold, and its blocks always carry a key glyph.

rules.note: v5 R1 (SPEC-v4 §9, the v5 R1 entry): every level has hold holding spaces, whatever its tag (v4.3 had Easy 6, Normal 5, Hard 4). Archers never kill on any level (archersKill is gone): a hit sapper is always knocked back and waits. The tag no longer changes any engine rule; it says how many features a level uses.

time.note: Engine timing (SPEC-v3 §3, the dispatch model), whole ms of engine time. A sapper sent at a pixel pops it yardMs + tiles x tileMs + biteMs later (tiles = its walk distance + 1) and is home yardMs + tiles x carryMs after that; a space sends one sapper every staggerMs; an archer hit lands halfway out and the sapper is back knockMs plus the walk later. The ratios shape which pixels squads claim, so changing them needs a rebake. To slow or speed the whole game without changing any outcome, turn show.pace instead. v4 M3 (the swarm): staggerMs 120 -> 30 so a big squad pours out (55 sappers leave in 1.6 s, not 6.6 s), biteMs 180 -> 100 and yardMs 250 -> 200 (less standing per block); the walk (tileMs, carryMs) is Peter's and unchanged.

flags.note: Comparison switch (SPEC-v3 §9, playtest 1). mergeLeftovers true: a tapped squad joins the space of its colour instead of taking its own (the old spam exploit). The bake assumes false.

twists.note: v4 M2 (SPEC-v4 §9). lockSpaces: how many of a lock level's last holding spaces start locked (never all of them), on every difficulty: Easy 6 -> 5 + lock, Normal 5 -> 4 + lock, Hard 4 -> 3 + lock. linkRowGap: E.check warns when linked partners are dealt more than this many rows apart.

v5.note: v5 R1 switches. relaid: false until R2 re-lays levels 1-100 under the v5 rules; while false, the checks that replay the shipped levels' stored orders and grades (tools/test.js, SP.selfTest, the regrades) are reported as DEFERRED, since those orders were dealt under v4.3's rules (6/5/4 spaces, lethal Hard archers).

freeze.note: v5 R1, the freeze test (tools/freeze.js): dir holds the frozen snapshot of shipped levels (frozen.json plus copies of the level files). After any engine change every level there must re-grade with 0 differences. Baselined at the end of R2 (tools/freeze.js --snapshot); until then the folder does not exist and the tool says so.

density.note: v5 R2, tags by feature density (the rules review: Easy uses few or none of the unlocked features, Normal more, Hard a lot, Extreme most or all; tools/tags.js densityOK). unlock: the level each feature arrives at (the feature ladder: moats 25, gates and keys 50, linked squads 75, mystery cards 100, archer towers 125, mystery blocks 150); no level uses a feature before it. easyMax: the most features an Easy level uses (and no lock); normalMin: the fewest a Normal level uses once that many are unlocked (no lock); a Hard level uses every unlocked feature and, from lockFrom, a locked space. A realm's first level teaches its new feature on an Easy level and may keep older ones.

locks.note: v5 R1: a locked holding space (a key lock or a colour lock; the level file says which) only on these tags, from this level on (tools/tags.js lockOK; R2 places them).

eras.name: Palisade stockade
eras.note: Log walls on an earth bank and ditch could go up in weeks, and forts like this were built for centuries.

eras.name: Motte and bailey
eras.note: The Normans raised hundreds of these after 1066: a timber tower on an earth mound over a fenced yard.

eras.name: Stone keep
eras.note: Stone replaced timber once a hold had to last. London's White Tower was begun about 1078.

eras.name: Concentric castle
eras.note: Walls within walls: Edward I's castles in Wales put a high inner curtain behind the outer one. Beaumaris was begun in 1295.

hidden.note: v5 R1, a mystery block on the board: a flat stud in c with a pixel ? (glyph rows, q its colour) filling size of the face; the same for every hidden block, so its colour never shows before it is exposed.

stud.note: v4 M1 flat stud: seam width in CSS px and its tone (the block's colour toward black), face corner radius (fraction of the face), a soft highlight band on the face's top (hi toward white, hiH of the face) and a faint foot (lo toward black, loH), and a small glint [x, y, w, h] as fractions of the face.

ring.note: Critics 1 fix: an archer ring at rest is a faint thin dash (quietW CSS px wide, quietDash CSS px, quietA alpha); it turns loud (rangeStroke, rangeW, rangeDash) while it matters: a colour the player can send now has a block in reach inside it, its archer shoots or just hit someone, or the coach points at a tower. fadeMs: the ease between the two.

crate.note: Critics 1 fix 2: an empty crate in the yard for each colour until its bin grows in (muted wood, no colour, so the yard at rest has content but no legend). scale: of the bin's size; planks: plank lines across it.

lockKey.note: v4 M2: the locked space's key block wears a mark in the holding line's socket colour (a gate's key wears a full ring in its gate's tint; Critics 1 fix: gate tints keep clear of cream and yellow), pulsing while the space is locked. Critics 1 fix: the mark is a dashed square, the locked space's own dashed rim, not corner brackets. w: line width, dash: [on, off], out: how far it sits outside the cell, all as a fraction of the cell.

pic.note: v4.1, picture boards: water is a flat stud in `water` with a `wave` across it (never a block); the entry square (the camp) is a dark gateway (`face`) with a lit `rim` along its sill in the frame's bottom row; v4.1 fix: under a timber gate (`timber`, `timberDark`: a lintel `lintel` of a cell tall across it, a post `post` of a cell wide at each end), with a dirt `path` from it into the yard, `pathRows` of the yard's rows long and `pathInset` of a cell in from the gate's ends. The archer stands on its tower's top row (archer.picLift above the row's middle).

show.note: Pacing (playtest 1). The page plays engine time (v3.time) at pace x real time, and x the speed button's multiplier (speeds: it cycles 1x, 2x, 3x; v4 M1); turning pace slows or speeds everything alike and changes no outcome. v4.3: the win or fail sheet waits until every sapper is home (settleCapMs, the old cap on that wait, is gone). maxRunners: sappers drawn at once (the rules never depend on it). v3.1: a refused tap (no free space) shakes its card for blockedShakeMs (blockedShake: px offsets) every time; its toast and blocked sound come at most once per blockedGapMs. victoryPace: once the tray is empty and the line is sure to win, the show plays at this pace (or the speed button's, if that is faster) until the sheet; presentation only.
show.pwNote: v4 M5: a power-up badge pops for pwPopMs when it is used or bought; the win's report counts its coins up over meta.report.countMs.

fx.note: Juice (M2): crumbs of the block's colour and a dust puff per popped pixel (sizes in cells, speeds in cells/s, gravity in cells/s^2, ms), the falling pops (gate bars, and the keep's last fx.winFallN pixels on the winning play), shakes [amplitude in cells, ms], and the coach's ring colour. Shakes are off under prefers-reduced-motion.

upright.note: v4.2 fix (the visual critic's B1): phones play upright. A touch screen (CSS pointer: coarse) held sideways (wider than tall) under maxH CSS px tall shows a full-screen card with text and pauses the game as a blur does; turning it upright hides the card and resumes. A desktop window or a portal's iframe on a desktop (pointer: fine) never shows it, whatever its shape. (layout.rotateBelowCss, the quarter-turned board, is gone: boards are always upright.)

layout.blockedText: No space: wait for a squad to finish
layout.twistsNote: v4 M2 twists on the page. linkedText: the toast for a refused linked tap. jamLinkedText / jamLockText: the jam sheet when a linked card needed 2 spaces, or a space was still locked. mystery: a hidden card's tile (colour c, text tc, glyph q; it never shows the card's colour or crew). rod: the bar joining linked tiles (width, stub length and gap in CSS px, colours). debugRow: the map's row of debug levels under ?debug=1. v4.3: linkedBuriedText, the toast (and a waiting card's aria) when a linked card's partner is not yet a front card; jamBuriedText, the jam sheet when linked fronts wait for buried partners. tags: each tag's mark on the map's buttons, the Gallery's tiles, the top bar and the report (empty: unmarked; Normal is), coloured by style.css .tag-<tag> (Hard a strong warning colour, Easy a calm one).
layout.jamLinkedText: Line jammed: linked squads need 2 free spaces
layout.linkedBuriedText: Linked squads go together: bring both to the front
layout.jamBuriedText: Line jammed: linked squads wait for partners buried in their columns
layout.fixNote: v4.3 fix pass. carryAria: the line head's return count (sappers carrying blocks home after their space freed). toastGapPx: on a wide screen a toast in play sits this far above the side column's tray.
layout.lockedText: Locked space: its key is on the board
layout.colourLockText: Locked space: opens when a {crew} squad goes out
layout.fixNote: Critics 1 fix. fade: the rows behind the front mix this share (t, per row) of the tray colour into their tile, in sRGB, never opacity (tools/fade.js: every faded tile stays ΔE00 20+ from every other colour it shows with); tray is the rail's stone (style.css --tray, set from here at boot); band (fix 2): row d sits on a band of the tray with this share of black mixed in (--band1, --band2), so the rows step back without touching the tile faces. minCellCss: the smallest board cell a coach band above the board may leave (else the coach sits in the top bar). hand: the coach's arrow; for a queue tile it comes in from the side at sideScale (its tip sideIn px inside the tile), for a space or the line from above (tip downIn px inside), and the line head's count steps aside by the arrow's half width (halfW) plus gap. rod: w, core and rivet (radius) in CSS px at a phone tile (52 px), scaled with the tile; partners two rows apart (and a partner below the visible rows: a stub of stub px and two dots) run down the gutter between their columns. mystery.c: the face-down card's back. jamChips: the most colour chips the jam sheet shows.
layout.m5Note: v4 M5. Short frames (CSS max-height shortRowsMaxH, e.g. the 400x600 iframe and landscape phones) show queueRowsShort rows so the power-up bar fits under the queue (orchestrator's call, 9/30); every other size keeps queueRows, unless a portrait board would then be under minCellCss CSS px a cell (then that level shows queueRowsShort and the compact bar). stageGapPx: the px kept free round the board's frame [across, down, down with two rows] (was 14 and 16 in code). pwGrid: on wide screens the bar lays its badges out 2x2 once the column's foot has this many CSS px of height and the badges come out bigger that way, else in a row; pwFit: the foot's fixed parts in CSS px (side padding, top padding, the coins header, bottom padding, a badge's name below it, the gap between rows and beside each badge) and the badge's min and max diameter.
layout.fix2Note: Critics 2 fix. coachTopFontPx: the coach in the top bar (only where neither three nor two queue rows leave the board minCellCss with the band above it) steps its font from the first to the second, one line, then two. rod.lane and rod.metal2 (m9): two rods down one gutter over the same rows take a lane each, lane px either side of its middle (scaled with the tile, never past the tiles' edges), the second in metal2.

teach.note: Coach scripts for the teaching levels (SPEC-v3 §5), by level id (v4.1: a teaching level is a castle picture whose material ids go by population, so a card pointer is that level's id for the lesson's colour; tools/teach-v4.js prints them for its build): one line over the board and a bouncing arrow on what to tap. A step ends when any `until` holds: play (a tap after the step showed), line (a space is taken), wait (a squad has more sappers waiting than pixels in reach), lineEmpty (every squad home), gate (every gate open), tower (every tower down), reach:m (colour m has a pixel in reach), used:m (a card of colour m was played), hit; v4 M3: reveal (a ? squad turned over), pair (a linked pair went out), unlock (the locked space opened), locked (it is still shut), hidden (a ? is in view), linkedFront (a front card is linked). v4 M3 pointers: mystery (a ? tile in view), linked (a linked front card), lockSlot (the padlocked space), ring lockKey (the space's key on the board). Critics 1 fix 2: short, the step's line where the coach sits in the top bar (a small screen where a band above the board would cost the board its 8 px cells). A step whose `if` fails when it comes up is skipped (the same words, plus short:m = the front card of m is bigger than what is in reach, and front:m = m is a front card). Pointers: card (the leftmost front card of that colour), next (a faded card behind a front one), line (the holding line; with a card it glows while the arrow points at the card), ring (key, gate or tower on the board). {n} {crew} {reach} {go} fill in from the pointed card ({go} = the smaller of the squad and what is in reach).

gallery.note: v4 M4, the Gallery (levels/gallery.json). openAt: the siege level whose clear opens it (v4.3: its first picture; the rest one at a time, seqNote). Text: title, btn, count ({n} won of {t}), lockedHint (on the locked buttons), winTitle, winLine ({title}), nextBtn. credits: the plain-text credits line under the grid (no links; the full list is LICENSES.md). thumbPx: canvas px a cell in the grid's thumbnails; dim: the dark and light ends a picture's lightness is squeezed into until it is won.
gallery.title: The Gallery
gallery.credits: Pictures: Twemoji by Twitter, Inc and other contributors (CC BY 4.0); Noto Emoji by Google (Apache 2.0); paintings and prints from The Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access (public domain); the rest are Click it! Studios originals.
gallery.fix2Note: Critics 2 fix (V2), the Gallery's payoff. A picture's first win says winLine (a repeat winLineAgain) and shows the finished picture above the report: reportCellPx CSS px a cell (whole device px), at most reportMaxPx tall, shrunk to the room on a small screen; under reportMinPx (a short landscape screen) it hangs over the razed board instead, at stageFrac of the board's frame (picAria its label). On the Gallery screen the first picture not yet cleared wears a gold frame and the playChip (nextAria; the others tileAria).
gallery.seqNote: v4.3: the pictures open one at a time: the first when openAt is cleared, each next when the one before it is cleared (save.js isOpen). A locked picture is a silhouette: its background cells (the colour its four corners share) in silhouette[1], the rest in silhouette[0], under a padlock; lockedAria is its label.
gallery.lockedAria: Picture {n}, locked: clear the one before it

meta.note: v4 M5, the meta layer (SPEC-v4 §9). lives: the lives system's switch (false on the web: plan Decision 2; turn it on for the app); livesMax, livesRefillMin (one life back per this many minutes, real time). coins: start (a new save's balance: enough to try each power-up once), win (coins per win by the level's tag; v4.3, by difficulty before) and first (added on the level's or picture's first clear; v4.3, a new medal before). pullDepth: how far behind the front the Quartermaster reaches (cards). powers: the four power-ups in engine order (engine.js PW), each with its price in coins and its uses per level (perLevel; the engine refuses past it).

speed.note: v5 R1, speed: every round starts at 1x. A player can buy x (2x) for the current attempt for price coins (Retry, a new level or leaving goes back to 1x; once bought the button toggles 1x and 2x free for that attempt). debugSpeeds: under ?debug=1 the button cycles these free (3x is a test tool only), and the debug speed carries over between levels. Nothing is saved (settings.speed is ignored). Texts: the buy sheet (say, buy, no), short (toast), bought (toast), label (the button's aria).

meta.unlockNote: v5 R1, power-up unlocks: each power-up (powers[k].unlockAt) appears once the player's campaign reaches that Siege level (the first open level not yet cleared; past the last, every one). Hidden before that, on every screen and level (the Gallery and debug levels follow the campaign), and the engine allows it no uses. On unlock it gets one free use (save got[id]) and its tip shows once (newTitle, free); every badge shows its tip on a long press (tipHoldMs) or a hover. tipIntroMs: how long the unlock tip stays (sim clock) unless tapped away.

cont.note: v5 R1, the continue on a jam (SPEC-v4 §9, the v5 R1 entry; engine revive()): offered on a jam's sheet when the engine would take it, once per attempt (perLevel; Retry gives a fresh one), for price coins. Every stuck squad finishes on the spot and play goes on. say: the offer's line; btn: its button; poor: the line when coins are short ({need}); short: the toast on a tap then; ad: the label for a future rewarded-ad button (main.js AD HOOK; no ad code yet).
cont.say: Every stuck squad finishes on the spot
cont.short: A continue costs {price}: you have {have} coins

powers.name: Ladder
powers.tip: One more holding space for this level. Use it when the line is nearly full of squads that are waiting.

powers.name: Quartermaster
powers.say: send any squad in view straight out
powers.tip: Sends any squad you can see straight into a free space. Use it to get a colour out ahead of the cards in front of it.

powers.name: Scout
powers.tip: Turns every ? squad face up. Use it when hidden squads make the next moves hard to plan.

powers.name: Recall
powers.tip: Sends a waiting squad back to the front of its column and frees its space. Use it when a stuck squad is blocking the line.

powers.name: Volley
powers.say: a catapult volley clears one colour
powers.tip: A catapult volley clears one colour from the fort, the queue and the line. Use it to break a jam nothing else can fix.

meta.textNote: The page's words for the meta layer. power: the power-up bar's toasts ({name}, {price}, {have}, {n}, {say}). report: the level report's rows ({v} a value, {n} coins). home: the home screen ({n} a level, {done} levels won, {t} total, {t} a countdown in lives). eraCard: the map's report card per era (and the Gallery's).
